content.user_title: Review COPPA Consent and Privacy Documentation
content.value_statement: Teams need to organize questions about audience classification, parental consent, and privacy documentation. This public guide frames those discussions and drafting requests for legal review.
actual_capabilities: Frames discussions about child-directed, mixed-audience, and general-audience service classification.
Describes separating baseline collection consent from third-party disclosure and targeted advertising consent.
Identifies retention policies, written security programs, and direct parental notices as drafting topics.
Highlights biometric and government identifiers as data inventory considerations.
Names Arkansas, Connecticut, and California as state overlay review topics.
Provides an illustrative math-game compliance question and response.
limitations: Only a public Markdown guide is included; scripts, extension source, and original package templates are absent.
No automated compliance checks, SDK configuration, or enforcement mechanisms are included.
Legal claims, deadlines, penalties, and the example classification require independent verification against current authoritative sources.
Coverage is limited to US COPPA and selected state topics, not GDPR-K or other international frameworks.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Audience Review
use_cases.description: Organize product facts and unresolved questions before counsel evaluates whether a game targets children or serves a mixed audience.

use_cases.title: Outline Consent Requirements
use_cases.description: Draft a review outline separating baseline collection from advertising disclosures before implementing an age screen or consent flow.

use_cases.title: Plan Privacy Documentation
use_cases.description: Identify inputs for retention policies, parental notices, and written security programs using a de-identified data inventory.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Review Topics
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this guide, list COPPA review topics for [service description]. Identify missing facts and avoid a definitive compliance conclusion.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Audience Questions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [audience and product facts]. Compare possible audience classifications, identify unresolved factors, and list questions for counsel without relying on age ranges alone.

prompt_templates.title: Outline Consent and Notices
prompt_templates.prompt: Using [de-identified data flows], outline separate consent decisions for collection, third-party disclosure, and advertising. Mark legal assumptions and missing parental notice inputs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare a consent design review.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Review Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Using [de-identified inventory] and [counsel-approved requirements], draft retention and security program outlines. Map gaps to owners and distinguish federal requirements from state considerations.

output_examples.input: Our math game serves ages 10 to 14 and uses an advertising SDK. What should we review first?
output: Audience classification: unresolved; age ranges alone do not establish mixed-audience status.
Collect product facts about visual design, content, marketing, intended users, and actual audience evidence.
Inventory SDK data collection and recipients before drafting consent requirements.
Have counsel verify the classification and applicable advertising disclosure rules.

output_examples.input: Outline a retention policy review for an EdTech service without sharing student records.
output: Inventory: list data categories, purposes, storage systems, and responsible owners.
Retention: identify proposed periods and unresolved legal or operational justifications.
Deletion: document proposed triggers, verification steps, and service-provider responsibilities.
Review status: draft for counsel; current requirements and implementation evidence remain unverified.

best_practices: Use de-identified product descriptions and data inventories instead of real child or parent records.
Verify legal statements against current FTC materials and applicable state law with qualified counsel.
Track assumptions and missing evidence separately from approved requirements and implemented controls.
anti_patterns: Treating the guide or generated drafts as legal certification or proof of compliance.
Classifying a service as mixed audience solely from the age range in the example.
Assuming the public guide includes paid templates, executable audits, or working SDK integrations.

faq.question: What is included in this skill?
faq.answer: One public Markdown guide describes COPPA review topics and an illustrative example. Original package scripts, extension source, and templates are not included.

faq.question: Does it certify COPPA compliance?
faq.answer: No. It supports discussion and drafting, not legal certification. Qualified counsel must verify requirements and review implementation evidence.

faq.question: Can it configure advertising SDKs or consent screens?
faq.answer: No implementation tooling is included. The guide describes consent concepts that can inform a separate engineering review.

faq.question: Does it cover international privacy laws?
faq.answer: No. The guide limits its scope to US COPPA and selected state topics, excluding GDPR-K and other international frameworks.

faq.question: Are its 2026 legal claims independently verified?
faq.answer: No. The file does not supply authoritative legal citations. Verify amendment dates, penalties, classifications, and obligations before relying on them.

faq.question: Should I provide real child or parent information?
faq.answer: Use de-identified inventories and product descriptions. These review tasks do not require actual child records, parent identifiers, or account credentials.
